docs.title: Selinexor and Pacritinib in JAK Inhibitor-naïve MF Patients With Cytopenias
docs.summary: This is a phase II, multicenter, open-label trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of pacritinib and selinexor in JAK inhibitor naïve patients with anemia and thrombocytopenia.

docs.title: A Trial to Compare Treatment With Surlorian (ARM210, S48168) to Placebo in Effects on Muscle Strength and Safety in Adults With Autosomal Dominant RYR1-related Myopathy
docs.summary: This study is testing a medicine called surlorian in adults who have a genetic muscle condition known as autosomal dominant RYR1-related myopathy (RYR1-RM). The goal is to find out whether surlorian improves muscle weakness, and whether it is safe and well tolerated.

docs.summary: Efficacy, safety and tolerability of switching from GLP-1RA to maridebart cafraglutide in adults with obesity or overweight.

docs.title: Firmonertinib in Perioperative Treatment of Resectable Stage II-IIIB EGFR-mutated Lung Adenocarcinoma
conditions: EGFR Positive Non-small Cell Lung Cancer
docs.summary:
An Open-label, Single-arm, Phase II Clinical Study of Firmonertinib in Perioperative Treatment of Resectable Stage II-IIIB EGFR-mutated Lung Adenocarcinoma.

The goal of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of firmonertinib neoadjuvant in patients with resectable stage II-IIIB EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) by major pathologic response (MPR).

docs.title: A Study to Investigate the Safety and Effectiveness of SAR448851 in Participants With Early Alzheimer's Disease
docs.summary:
This is a randomized, placebo-controlled Phase 2 study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of SAR448851 in early Alzheimer's disease (AD) participants. The purpose of this study is to measure efficacy and safety with once daily oral SAR448851 compared to placebo in participants with mild cognitive impairment due to AD or mild AD dementia and with evidence of cerebral amyloid pathology.

docs.summary:

The goal of this study is to evaluate the effect of various doses of ABBV-295 compared to placebo on reducing body weight at Week 32 in participants with obesity or overweight with weight-related comorbidities.

docs.title: Combination Bevacizumab and PRGN-2012 in Adults With Recurrent Respiratory Papillomatosis (RRP)
docs.summary:
Background:

Recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP) is a rare disease that causes wart-like growths called papillomas to grow in the airway, most often in the voice box, windpipe, or lungs. These growths can make it hard to speak or breathe. Surgery can remove the papillomas, but they often come back. In some cases, they can become cancerous.

Objective:

This study istesting whether two treatments used together (PRGN-2012, a vaccine-based treatment and bevacizumab, a drug that affects blood vessel growth) can help control RRP and reduce the chance that papillomas will grow back.

docs.title: AV-1959R Vaccine in Individuals With Preclinical Alzheimer's Disease
docs.summary: This Phase 2 study will evaluate the safety, tolerability, immunogenicity, and amyloid-lowering effect of AV-1959R in cognitively unimpaired adults with preclinical Alzheimer's disease. Approximately 160 participants will be randomized to receive AV-1959R or placebo and will be followed for 78 weeks. The study will assess safety, immune responses, brain amyloid, and Alzheimer's disease-related biomarkers.

docs.title: Study to Assess the Effect and Safety of ALV-100 on Maintenance of Weight Loss
docs.summary: A study of ALV-100 to assess efficacy, safety and tolerability among participants with overweight or obesity who have previously achieved a body weight reduction of ≥10% while treated with incretin-based therapies.

docs.title: SYNCHRONIZE®-START- A Study to Test Whether Survodutide Helps People Living With Overweight or Obesity Who do Not Have Diabetes to Lose Weight
docs.summary:
This study is open to adults with overweight or obesity. People can join the study if they have a body mass index (BMI) of 30 kg/m² or more, or a BMI of 27 kg/m² or more with at least one weight- related health problem. Participants must not have diabetes, and they must have tried to lose weight by dieting at least once in the past without success. The purpose of this study is to find out whether a medicine called survodutide helps people with overweight or obesity lose weight.

docs.summary:

A new formulation of this drug, called GE-287, has been developed. This new formulation may offer advantages for patient tolerability and can be produced more reliably and efficiently.

docs.title: A Study of PLS240 in Pediatric Participants With Secondary Hyperparathyroidism and Chronic Kidney Disease on Hemodialysis
docs.summary:
Approximately 56 participants who are 1 month old to 17 years old will be enrolled in this study. The total duration for this study will be 38 weeks (or up to 42 weeks when participants require a washout period due to prior exposure to prohibited medications) and includes the following periods:

* Active screening period of 6 weeks (or, up to 10 weeks for participants requiring a washout period).
* Treatment period of 28 weeks consisting of a 19-week dose titration period and 9-week stable dose period.
* Safety follow-up period of 4 weeks.

docs.title: Lean Mass Changes With Semaglutide in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes and Overweight/Obesity.
docs.sponsor: McGill University Health Centre/Research Institute of the McGill University Health Centre
docs.summary:
The goal of this 24 week double-blinded, randomized, parallel controlled clinical trial is to learn how semaglutide affects body composition in adults with type 1 diabetes and overweight/obesity.

The main question to answer is:

What effect does Semaglutide have on body composition in adults with type 1 diabetes and overweight/obesity compared to a placebo?

Around 40 participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to receive semaglutide or a placebo.
* Self-administer the treatment drug once per week for 24 weeks.
* Complete a series of tests, measurements and questionnaires throughout the study

docs.title: Reducing Arterial Inflammation Using Eplerenone and Statins in HIV
docs.summary: HIV has transitioned to a chronic disease in which well-treated persons remain at higher risk for heart disease when compared to the general population. Statin medications have been shown to reduce the number of events related to heart disease, but there are still individuals who will have complications from heart disease despite statin use. This study is being conducted to determine whether adding on another medication to statins called eplerenone, which has been shown to reduce inflammation in the heart vasculature among persons with HIV, can further decrease the risk of heart disease in HIV

docs.title: Efficacy And Safety of Olatorepatide in Adults With Overweight or Obesity Without Diabetes
docs.summary:
This study will test olatorepatide (study drug) to determine whether it can help treat overweight or obesity.

In this study we will test how safe and how well olatorepatide works compared to placebo in people who are overweight or obese but do not have diabetes.

The study is looking at:

* How well the study drug works
* How the body and blood and urine biomarkers change after taking the study drug, which can help researchers understand why the study drug may work better in some people than in others
* What side effects the study drug might cause

docs.title: Pucotenlimab and Anlotinib in Combination With Chemotherapy
docs.summary: A prospective, multicenter, single-arm clinical study enrolling patients with histologically confirmed invasive carcinoma, clinical stage II-III, known PD-L1 status, and treatment-naïve triple-negative breast cancer. Patients will receive neoadjuvant therapy with pucotenlimab, anlotinib, and nab-paclitaxel, sequentially followed by epirubicin and cyclophosphamide, for a total of 8 cycles.

docs.title: Investigating the Effects of 24 Hour LEAP2 Infusion in Individuals With Overweight and Obesity
docs.summary:

docs.title: A Study of MDSY-1240, a STAT3 Degrader, for the Treatment of Hematologic Malignancies and Advanced Solid Tumors
conditions: Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (HNSCC) - Recurrent/Metastatic (R/M)
docs.summary:
This clinical trial is evaluating a drug called MDSY-2140 in participants with hematologic malignancies and advanced solid tumors. The main goals of this study are to:

* Find the recommended dose of MDSY-1240 that can be safely given to participants
* Learn more about the side effects and effectiveness of MDSY-1240
